item.title: 40% of premium bread bakers shut down in 2yrs
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole At the backdrop of difficulties in the economic environment, about 40 percent of bread-makers operating in the premium category, have shut their factories in the past three years. This was revealed by the Premium Breadmakers Association of Nigeria (PBAN) attributing the situation to rising energy costs, poor access to affordable financing and inadequate government support. They warned that the challenges were threatening the survival of businesses and jobs in the sector. PBAN President, Engr. Emmanuel Onuorah, speaking on the sidelines of PBAN’s 2026 Day-Out event in Lagos yesterday, said the association’s theme, “Baking Through the Economic Storm: Innovation, Efficiency and Growth for a Sustainable Industry”, reflected the difficult operating environment and the need for innovation, creativity and efficiency to sustain the industry. He said: “The past years have been very tough. Words cannot even express how we feel. Our businesses are struggling, businesses are going down, and members are closing. In the last two years, we have lost close to 40 per cent of our membership to economic pressures. “Energy is killing businesses. We are trying to innovate, be creative and improve efficiency because, without efficiency, there is no way we can remain in business.” Onuorah, a petroleum engineer with 25 years’ experience in the oil and gas industry, said the association was exploring alternative energy sources, including a hybrid system that would allow bakeries to switch between diesel and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG). However, he put the cost of transitioning a small bakery to the hybrid system at between N40 million and N50 million, describing the huge capital requirement and inadequate CNG supply as major obstacles. He also disclosed that PBAN had explored solar energy solutions but abandoned the initiative after discovering that the proposed financing arrangements would cost more than what members currently paid for electricity. The PBAN president faulted the financial system for failing to provide affordable credit to businesses in the real sector, alleging that government-backed intervention loans were largely inaccessible to genuine operators. According to him, even when sought for a loan of N12 million to convert lighting and air-conditioning systems at his facility to solar-powered alternatives, the bank was asking for a 34 per cent interest rate and a 20 per cent counterpart funding requirement. “How do you expect small businesses to survive with interest rates of 34 per cent? We are not asking for free money. We are asking for single-digit interest rates that businesses can realistically repay,” he said. He also questioned the effectiveness of government intervention programmes for small businesses, arguing that politically connected individuals benefited more than genuine entrepreneurs. item.title: 2027 polls: NASS condemns electoral violence nationwide
item.description: By Henry Umoru & Gift ChapiOdekina ABUJA- AHEAD of 2027 general elections, the National Assembly has condemned the wave of political violence across the country. Read Also: * Who won Lagos in 2023? * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal While the Senate urged the security agents to apprehend whoever was culpable in such acts to serve as deterrent to others, the House of Reps resolved to investigate the attacks. Speaking with Vanguard, yesterday, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Media and Public Affairs, Senator Yemi Adaramodu(APC, Ekiti South), said: “President Bola Tinubu is preaching peace and national harmony, the National Assembly is in support of Mr President on this. “We thus condemn in totality any act of political violence and urge the security agents to apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act.” Meanwhile, the Reps in its resolution, sequel to the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by the House Minority Leader, Mr. Fred Agbedi, and 16 other lawmakers, expressed concern over attacks on political meetings, rallies and processions in different parts of the country. In Katsina State recently, supporters of the All Progressives Congress, APC, travelling for a campaign flag-off in Funtua were reportedly attacked along the Yashi-Funtua route in October. A female member of the party was injured, vehicles were damaged, and the police subsequently announced 14 arrests. Also in Calabar, Cross River State, the convoy of the presidential candidate of the NDC, Peter Obi, was attacked on November 4, 2026. Police confirmed damage to vehicles and announced the arrest of a suspect, while investigations continued. On November 7, 2026, one person was killed and five others injured during an attack on a political procession and rally organised by supporters of NDC, along Nnebisi Road in Asaba, Delta State. This came as the National Peace Committee said it recorded 60 election-related incidents within one month, including violence, intimidation and threats. At yesterday plenary, presenting the motion on behalf of the sponsors, Agbedi condemned acts of violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property associated with political rallies, meetings, processions and other lawful political activities, irrespective of the political parties or individuals affected. He appealed to political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and cooperate with security agencies in maintaining public peace. Citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Minority Leader reminded lawmakers that Nigerians were guaranteed the right to assemble freely and associate with others, including the right to form or belong to political parties. item.title: Wike targets 3m votes for Tinubu in Rivers
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike, has inaugurated the Presidential Campaign Council for Rivers State, directing members to recruit at least five new voters daily to secure victory for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election. Wike, who inaugurated the council on Thursday, set a target of three million votes for Tinubu in the state, urging members to work hard, remain focused and pursue issue-based campaigns. He dismissed concerns over confusion surrounding appointments into the various committees, saying the list of chairmen and members of the subcommittees would be ready by Monday to enable them to commence work. “I am sure by Monday the list of the chairmen and members of the various subcommittees will have been prepared so that the chairmen can kick-start by inviting their various committee members. It is very important,” he said. Wike expressed confidence in the president’s victory in Rivers, declaring that the task before the council was to secure the targeted votes. “Everybody knows that we are going to win election in Rivers State. So we are not talking about winning now,” he said. Recalling a discussion with Senate President Godswill Akpabio on the three-million-vote target, Wike said he had assured him that the figure was achievable through hard work. “He said, ‘How much is the registered votes here?’ I said, ‘over three million.’ He said, ‘Okay, you will bring three million.’ I said, ‘Well, we will try’. I know that three million, if we work hard, it is easy,” he recalled. The minister urged council members to see their appointments as an opportunity to work for the Rainbow Coalition, stressing the need for unity and discipline in the face of opposition provocations. He cited the position of the Olubadan of Ibadanland and former Oyo State governor, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, who reportedly expressed support for the coalition during a courtesy visit by the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, National Working Committee. Wike said Ladoja had indicated that, but for his position as a traditional ruler, he would have joined the Rainbow Coalition, which he described as a platform for bringing together different political interests to secure Tinubu’s re-election. In his remarks, Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, described the new campaign council as bigger, wider and better coordinated than the structure that secured victory for Tinubu in 2023. He said former political adversaries had now closed ranks to work together for the state and the President. “Nothing is impossible. The only thing that is not possible is to revive the dead. If we take this as a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out decisively with a stronger vote than what we did in 2023,” Fubara said. Fubara assured members who were not included in the initial appointments that they would be accommodated in the subcommittees. item.title: Tompolo leads grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu in Jigawa, Zamfara
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA—Grand Patron of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, PBAT, Door-to-Door Movement, Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has led a drive to mobilise voters for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in Jigawa and Zamfara states, unveiling 56 campaign vehicles for the two chapters. The vehicles, 31 for Jigawa and 25 for Zamfara, were unveiled on Thursday at the inauguration of the Movement’s state chapters. Tompolo was represented at both events by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services, Chief Kestin Pondi. Pondi said the vehicles were meant to ease transportation challenges and help members reach more communities with information on the policies and achievements of the Tinubu administration. He said they would be placed under the control of the governors. Jigawa State Governor Umar Namadi and his Zamfara State counterpart, Dauda Lawal, joined Tompolo’s team in urging voters in both states to turn out massively for the President in 2027. Jigawa pledged to deliver two million votes. Namadi said the state remained firmly behind Tinubu’s second-term ambition. He described the 31 vehicles as a major boost to mobilisation and urged members to use them judiciously. The governor challenged party supporters to turn their enthusiasm into votes, reminding them of the state’s earlier commitment of two million votes for the President. Pondi thanked Jigawa residents for the turnout during Tinubu’s recent visit, which he described as a show of confidence in the President’s leadership. He urged them to vote for Tinubu and Namadi in 2027, insisting that both deserve another four years. He recalled that Jigawa and Zamfara were among the states that contributed significantly to Tinubu’s victory in the last presidential election, and urged residents to surpass that performance. Pondi also appealed to Nigerians to be patient with the administration’s economic reforms, saying the benefits would take time to reach individual households. He said the economy was stabilising and that state governments now had more resources to execute projects and pay workers’ salaries. In Zamfara, Lawal thanked Tompolo and the Movement for backing the President’s re-election campaign. He urged the state leadership of the Movement to take charge of its operations and promised the support of his administration, declaring that Zamfara was for the All Progressives Congress (APC). The National Coordinator of the Movement, Comrade Sunday Adekanbi Asuku, commended the people and leaders of both states for their support. He urged eligible voters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and take part actively in the general elections. Asuku told Zamfara leaders that Nigeria had the right people in positions at both national and state levels, a situation he described as unprecedented since the return of democracy. item.title: Lagos APC rally: Sanwo-Olu, Ambode, others, seek voters’ support for Tinubu, Hamzat
item.description: By Clifford Ndujihe & Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor, Mr. Babajide Sanwo-Olu and his predecessor, Akinwunmi Ambode have applauded President Bola Tinubu’s contributions to Lagos’ development, urging residents to show appreciation for his infrastructural interventions by re-electing him for a second term in 2027. The duo, who spoke while addressing party faithful and mmmoth crowd, at the Lagos All Progressives Congress, APC, East Senatorial District Rally, held on Thursday, at the Epe Recreational Ground, Epe, said President Tinubu had laid a solid foundation for Lagos State over two decades ago, providing the blueprint for the state’s sustained growth and development. According to him, “The President deserves more than our votes. He deserves our prayers and our support. I therefore urged Lagos residents to demonstrate your appreciation for the President’s leadership by turning out in large numbers on January 16 to express your support and vote massively for him.” The governor added that Lagos had become one of Africa’s most sought-after city-states through deliberate policies, strategic planning and visionary leadership initiated under the President’s political and administrative stewardship. Sanwo-Olu observed that the President’s transition from Lagos to the national stage had provided an opportunity to replicate his development philosophy across Nigeria, with ongoing interventions and projects cutting across the six geopolitical zones. Similarly, the Deputy Governor, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, KOH, said the purpose of the campaign visit to the district was to canvass support for all APC candidates, urging residents to come out en masse on election day to vote rather than stay at home. He noted that President Tinubu had recorded significant achievements in infrastructure, education, healthcare and other critical sectors, stressing the need for residents to support the continuation of the administration’s development efforts. “On election day, let us not stay at home. Come out with your PVC and ensure that everyone in your neighbourhood votes. We have the highest number of registered voters in Nigeria. “Let us come out to vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and every candidate that will support the continuity of his good work,” Hamzat said. Senator representing Lagos East Senatorial District, Senator Tokunbo Abiru, urged residents to demonstrate their appreciation for the President’s efforts by supporting his re-election for a second term, adding that the state had capable leaders to sustain the administration’s development agenda. Ambode stressed the APC’s consistency and longstanding presence in Lagos politics, noting that the party had remained committed to its political identity rather than moving between political platforms. item.title: City Boy Movement holds outreach for vulnerable, urges support for Tinubu
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – THE City Boy Movement through its City Boy care has organized an outreach for some segments of the society where the Edo State Coordinator of the Movement and All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Oredo Federal Constituency, Dr. Paddy Iyamu reaffirmed the organisation’s commitment to improving the welfare of the people through meaningful interventions. He said that its activities were driven by the desire to positively impact lives. The outreach programme was powered by Pipeline Infrastructure Ltd and some of the beneficiaries included pregnant women, students and other vulnerable groups with various support packages, including assistance for beneficiaries in need of healthcare services. Iyamu said the movement remained committed to its slogan of informing, engaging and empowering the people, stressing that its interventions were designed to improve the lives of beneficiaries. He noted that the latest outreach featured interventions for pregnant women, students benefiting from the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) scheme and individuals requiring medical assistance. “We care a lot about humanity. “This is not about elections, vote-buying or canvassing for votes. It is a drive to ensure that we leave people better than the way we met them,” he said. Iyamu urged residents to continue supporting the government and praying for President Bola Tinubu and Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo and commended the organisers, volunteers and management of the host facility for their contributions to the success of the outreach. Speaking on the initiative, the Director of City Boy Care, Omowunmi Imoukuede, said the organisation’s intervention in Edo State was motivated by its commitment to humanitarian service and continuity in governance rather than electoral considerations. She described President Bola Tinubu as the movement’s original City Boy and reaffirmed its commitment to demonstrating love and support for residents through various interventions. Also speaking, the Chief Medical Director of Edo Specialist Hospital, Dr. Anthonia Inibokun Njoku, commended the City Boy Care team, particularly its young volunteers, for their dedication and contributions to the outreach. One of the beneficiaries, Mrs. Blessing Osebor, expressed gratitude to the organisers for the support extended to the pregnant women, describing the intervention as timely and generous. item.title: Italy stun France 3-1 to hand Zidane first defeat as Les Bleus coach
item.description: Italy came from behind to beat France 3-1 in Milan and hand Zidane his first defeat since taking charge of Les Bleus. France were without Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele due to injury but Michael Olise pounced on a loose pass from Gianluigi Donnarumma to fire them ahead on 10 minutes. Francesco Pio Esposito steered in Nicolo Cambiaghi’s pass to bring Italy level before France twice hit the post through Bradley Barcola and Rayan Cherki. Sebastiano Esposito blazed a second-half penalty wide for Italy, but Roberto Mancini’s side did not rue that miss as Davide Frattesi powered home Federico Dimarco’s cut-back. Francesco Pio Esposito then doubled his tally for the night, succeeding where his older brother had failed by converting a penalty after Dayot Upamecano fouled substitute Antonio Vergara. Italy climbed above France at the top of Group A1 on head-to-head record. Both teams have 10 points going into the final round of games, with Belgium just one point adrift. Belgium host Italy on Sunday and France are at home to Turkey. Turkey slid to a fifth straight loss as they went down 2-1 to Belgium in Izmir. Arda Guler’s magnificent free-kick put Turkey ahead under new coach and former midfielder Sergen Yalcin, but Belgium struck twice in quick succession with goals from Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere to come away with victory. item.title: US Congress Steps Up Scrutiny Of Trump, Nvidia After Huang Exit
item.description: Key US lawmakers on Thursday called for clarity on what the Trump administration knew about Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, after the AI chip giant announced his departure. Huang, now Nvidia’s former CEO, had pushed for looser rules on sales of US chips to China — crucial in the AI race — and the controversy has reenergized advocates of a hard line on Beijing, days before Donald Trump travels to China. “Despite Jensen Huang’s resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put US national security at risk,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said on social media. “The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset,” he added. Huang, a co-founder of the AI chip giant, on Sunday acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence suspects her of working for Beijing, which has strongly denied the allegations. ‘Obvious Threat’ According to The New York Times, Trump was informed of the suspicions last year, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed them to him in May. Trump said on Monday he knew “the FBI is looking into” the affair, adding that he expected Huang to be “in good shape.” He said Huang had told him he did not know the woman was a spy. U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP Huang was ultimately brought down by the scandal on Thursday, when the company’s board announced his departure, effective immediately. Lawmakers are also raising questions about Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged reluctance to impose restrictions on exports of the chips to China. Three Republican House committee chairmen had already said they wanted to hear from Huang behind closed doors on November 18. Democrats, who will take control of both chambers of Congress in January after winning the midterm elections, have also said they intend to look more closely into the affair. The top Democrats on the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means committees told Lutnick in a letter on Thursday that they were investigating the administration’s “scheme to approve and tax” Nvidia chip exports to Chinese firms linked to Beijing’s government and military. They accuse Lutnick and Trump of ignoring the “obvious national security threat” posed by the ties between Huang and a suspected Chinese intelligence agent, even though they had reportedly been informed of them. item.title: Spain beat Czech Republic to retain perfect Nations League record
item.description: Alex Baena scored from the spot and Marc Pubill added another seconds from time as Spain beat ten-men Czech Republic 2-0 in the Nations League in Prague on Thursday. The win leaves Spain unbeaten in 44 competitive games in a row, including five wins in as many Nations League games this season. Spain, who already secured a quarter-final berth before travelling to Prague, will face England in Madrid on Sunday in their final Group A3 game. Baena scored on 39 minutes after a VAR check revealed Czech midfielder Lukas Ambros had handled the ball inside the box. The Atletico Madrid winger blasted his spot kick past Matej Kovar who touched the ball but failed to clear it. Czech captain Ladislav Krejci was sent off in the 69th minute after bringing down second-half substitute Roberto Fernandez on a counter-attack. It was a deja-vu for the Wolverhampton defender who also got a red card at the end of Spain’s 3-1 home win over the Czechs last month. Pubill, another substitute, beat Kovar with a low shot deep into stoppage time after the Czech back four left him alone facing the Eindhoven goalkeeper. Luis de la Fuentes missed Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Rodri and Eric Garcia over injuries while Mikel Oyarzabal was sidelined with flu for the Prague game. Spain got off to a slow start on the chilly evening but never really let the hosts get close throughout the first half. They gradually stepped up their pressure, often confining the Czechs to their box and looking for chances. Fabian Ruiz hit the post with a curling right-footer three minutes from halftime, while Dean Huijsen’s header found Kovar’s arms. Yeremy Pino, replacing Yamal on the right flank, saw his goal overturned by VAR for offside just two minutes into the second half. The Czechs showed higher spirits after the break, but David Zima tipped the ball over the bar from close range on 50 minutes and Adam Hlozek’s glancing header landed on the top of the crossbar. The Czechs lost momentum after the red card, but Baena had two efforts cleared by Kovar who also denied Fernandez from close range. The hosts, led by de la Fuente’s long-time collaborator Santi Denia, have lost all their Nations League games this season. They are next travelling to Croatia for a game they need to win to stay in the top tier of the competititon for the next edition. item.title: Record-breaking Kane fires England into Nations League knockouts
item.description: Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking 126th England appearance with a goal from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 on Thursday to book a place in the Nations League quarter-finals. Slaven Bilic’s team were determined to avoid the embarrassment of their 7-0 mauling by England in Rijeka last month and looked much more solid from the kick-off. But goals from Morgan Rogers and captain Kane kept England second in their group, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March. Neither side got out of second gear in the opening stages of the match at Wembley. Elliot Anderson fired over in the 16th minute and Croatia’s Josip Misic flashed a shot wide midway through the first half. Chelsea forward Rogers broke the deadlock in the 24th minute in slightly fortuitous fashion following a neat move by the home side. Kane floated a ball to Jude Bellingham on the right of the penalty area and the Real Madrid man cushioned the ball first time across the area towards Rogers. Manchester City’s Josko Gvardiol had a chance to clear but got in a tangle and Chelsea’s Rogers poked the ball past goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic. England started to find some rhythm as they went in search of a second goal but failed to add to their tally before half-time. Thomas Tuchel’s men were again the more potent team at the beginning of the second period. But the visitors levelled against the run of play just before the hour mark after a glaring error by England defender Jarell Quansah, who misdirected a header from close range towards Jordan Pickford following a Croatia corner. The ball fell to Petar Sucic, who stabbed home. Minutes later England were back in front, with Bayer Leverkusen defender Quansah again at the heart of the action after his shirt was tugged in the penalty area. Referee Morten Krogh initially did not award a penalty but he was sent to the monitor by the VAR and pointed to the spot. Kane made no mistake, drilling home for record-extending 92nd England goal. Nikola Vlasic gave England a scare, firing just wide of Jordan Pickford’s goal as Croatia showed they were still alive. James Garner thought he had scored a third for England after a Bellingham cut-back but Bellingham was in an off-side position when he received the ball. Ballon d’Or winner Kane won his 126th cap when the game kicked off — taking him clear of his tie with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton. A giant banner was raised before kick-off with a picture of the 33-year-old and the words “England’s Finest”. Shilton was part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions skipper, along with Football Association patron Prince William. England remain second in Nations League Group A3, after leaders Spain beat the Czech Republic 2-0 but are now assured of a place in the quarter-finals. item.title: Online safety concerns are reshaping how people meet strangers
item.description: It’s hard to ignore how meeting new people online has changed in the past decade. With so many platforms connecting millions, the possibilities feel endless, but the risks have become more visible too. Stories about scams, harassment, and data breaches are everywhere, and they’ve made people think twice before reaching out to someone they don’t know. Safety concerns aren’t just in the background anymore—they’re shaping the way we start conversations, choose platforms, and decide how much to share. As awareness grows, so do new habits and expectations for digital introductions. This shift doesn’t just affect individuals; it’s influencing whole communities as we all adapt to a more cautious, connected world. Changing first steps: why some users now engage with strangers differently online That growing caution is easy to spot in the way people now approach first interactions with strangers online. Instead of jumping right into open conversations, many start by looking for platforms that let them control who they talk to, or give them the option to remain anonymous until they feel comfortable. Features like one-click exit buttons, video previews, or private chat rooms have become popular for exactly this reason. Women, in particular, are leading this change. They’re more likely to say safety is a top concern, which shows up in everything from avoiding certain apps to using aliases or insisting on in-app messaging only. The choice of platform matters too. Video chat sites, for example, offer a sense of control because users can see and hear who they’re talking to—and can leave the conversation instantly if something doesn’t feel right. For many, getting to know LuckyCrush and similar services is part of this shift toward safer, more controlled first steps when meeting someone new. It’s a sign that concerns are not stopping people from connecting, but are changing the rules for how those first moments happen. a shift in trust: navigating caution in the age of digital introductions That change in first steps is really about trust—how it’s built, how it’s lost, and why it matters so much now. People aren’t just jumping into conversations and sharing details the way they might have a decade ago. Instead, there’s this sense of needing to pause and check for warning signs. With more stories surfacing about online fraud and harassment, it feels riskier to let your guard down. A lot of users now watch for inconsistent stories, pressure to move chats off-platform, or requests for private information as red flags that something isn’t right. Some of the ways people protect themselves include sticking to messaging within the app, looking for verification badges, or even googling someone before agreeing to meet. These habits are becoming more common, especially as platforms roll out tools designed for safer interactions. The numbers back up this shift in attitude. item.title: UNN Deaths: Gov Mbah mourns, orders investigation
item.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr Peter Mbah, has expressed deep grief over the deaths of four students of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, UNN, who reportedly died during an off-campus sign-out party organised for one of their friends, describing the incident as a heartbreaking loss. Mbah described the deaths as a grievous loss, not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to Enugu State as a whole. He called for a ban on sign-out parties among undergraduates, noting that the practice had brought too much sorrow to families and tertiary institutions across the country. This was contained in a press statement issued by the governor’s media aide, Mazi Uche Anichukwu, on Thursday. “I received with rude shock and deep sense of loss the news of the off-campus sign-out party leading to the death of four students of the University of Nigeria Nsukka, and hospitalisation of six others. “This is a grievous loss not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to us as a state. Losing them in their prime and along with their promising future cuts as deeply as a sharp knife. We, therefore share in this grief and pray God to grant their families, friends, and the UNN community the equanimity to bear the heartbreaking loss. “Our hearts go out to their parents in particular, who sacrificed personal comforts to sponsor their children through the university, but only to face this sad turn of events. “As a government, we have ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding their deaths and will work closely with the university authorities and security agencies to get to the roots of the sad development and forestall a recurrence. “In the meantime, I have suspended my scheduled town hall meeting with the UNN community on Friday, November 13, 2026, as we join the university in mourning the dead. “Going forward, we will work with the authorities of tertiary institutions to enforce a full ban on sign-out parties and other excessive celebrations, a trend that has cost more lives and brought more sorrows than joy to families and higher institutions of learning,” the governor stated. Mbah also called for increased public enlightenment campaigns by relevant agencies and institutions on the consequences of drug use and abuse. He prayed for the peaceful repose of the souls of the deceased. The post UNN Deaths: Gov Mbah mourns, orders investigation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘His Support Base Still Strong’, Doherty Says Obi Can Repeat 2023 Feat In Lagos
item.description: The Lagos governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, says the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, retains a strong support base and has the backing to repeat his 2023 electoral performance in Lagos State. Doherty said this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, following an attack on the party’s town hall meeting in Lagos. He dismissed suggestions that Obi’s reception among Nigerians could be weakened by his defection from the Labour Party to the NDC, arguing that his appeal is rooted in his political philosophy rather than the platform on which he contests elections. “The idea of a new party is not something that we should hang our hat on anymore in our clime. Parties may be new, but the individuals involved are not new. “But the reception of Peter Obi today, that is how it is everywhere he goes. This is a man who is loved by the people. They view him as a different kind of politician, for good reason, and those of us who align with that philosophy and thinking,” he said. Doherty warned against underestimating Obi’s political influence, saying such an assumption could prove costly. “Anybody who is making a contrary case, time will tell. But I would advise them that if they are saying that just to downplay his significance, I think it will be a grave mistake on their part because his support base is still strong. I have seen it, not just today, we have seen it multiple times,” he added. He said the resistance by NDC supporters to the disruption of the party’s town hall meeting was evidence that the enthusiasm which characterised Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign had not diminished. “Those guys came in today probably thinking they would have an easy ride of it. They would come in and do what they might normally do, scatter things and people would run away. But people were not in that frame of mind. “We have laboured for this, and you cannot deprive us of it. And I think that spirit is alive and strong. To those who might think that, following 2023, people have lost some of that energy, I think, if anything, today should let us know that it is game on.” Attack On NDC supporters An injured NDC supporter during the attack by suspected thugs in Lagos Doherty also condemned the attack on the party’s town hall meeting at Classic Event Place in Oregun, Ikeja, describing it as “unprovoked” and “unnecessary.” Suspected political thugs invaded the venue on Thursday ahead of the arrival of Obi and his supporters. The attackers, said to be armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones, allegedly vandalised property and damaged several vehicles parked within the premises. However, NDC supporters resisted the attackers, confronting them and throwing chairs in an attempt to drive them away. The confrontation disrupted activities at the venue before security operatives intervened. item.title: My Ambition Is To Ensure Tinubu’s 2027 Victory, Says Matawalle
item.description: The Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, says his major ambition is to ensure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections. Matawalle made this known while addressing supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) at his residence in Gusau, Zamfara State, ahead of the expected visit of the First Lady, Senator Remi Tinubu. He urged party members to unite and intensify mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election, as well as the victory of other APC candidates in the state. The minister commended Tinubu’s efforts in tackling insecurity, developing infrastructure and promoting political cohesion, expressing his commitment to ensuring that the President completes his eight-year tenure. Matawalle said that after discharging his responsibilities as Minister of State for Defence, particularly in the fight against insecurity, his next major priority would be to work towards Tinubu’s re-election. He also dismissed what he described as provocations and propaganda by individuals seeking to tarnish his image, insisting that his priority was to sustain unity within the APC in Zamfara and secure victories for the party at all levels. The minister further dismissed allegations and propaganda concerning Tinubu’s health, maintaining that the President was fit to continue providing leadership and direction for the country. On security, Matawalle assured Zamfara residents that the Federal Government would deploy additional security personnel along major highways to protect commuters from persistent bandit attacks. He specifically mentioned the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway, as well as the Gummi-Anka-Bukkuyum and Tsafe access roads, as routes that would receive increased security attention. “We will deploy security forces along the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway to ensure the safe movement of commuters. We will also deploy security personnel to ensure the safety of those travelling along the Gummi, Anka, Bukkuyum and Tsafe roads,” he said. Matawalle pledged to do everything within his capacity to address insecurity in Zamfara and other parts of the country. He also spoke on the controversy surrounding the rerun election in Zamfara North Senatorial District, dismissing allegations of attempts to undermine his political standing and create divisions within the APC. The minister questioned the rationale behind the violence reportedly recorded during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji, insisting that political disagreements should not lead to attacks or destruction. “Those who caused the crisis during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji know whether they can emerge victorious or not. If victory is on your side, what is the essence of creating a crisis? We will not fight or attack anybody,” he said. item.title: 2027: ‘Arrest perpetrators’, Senate condemns political violence nationwide
item.description: By Henry Umoru AHEAD of 2027 Presidential and general elections, the Senate has condemned in very strong terms, cases of political violence, attacks and disruption of political activities across the country. The Senate has thus taken a swipe at acts of violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property associated with political rallies, meetings, processions and other lawful political activities, irrespective of the political parties or individuals affected. The Senate has urged the security agents to as a matter of urgency apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act in order to serve as deterrent to others. The Upper Chamber has called on all political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and cooperate with security agencies in maintaining public peace. Speaking with Vanguard yesterday, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Media and Public Affairs, Senator Yemi Adaramodu, APC, Ekiti South, said, “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is preaching peace and national harmony, the National Assembly is in support of Mr President on this. “We thus condemn in totality any act of political violence and urge the security agents to apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act.” Vanguard News The post 2027: ‘Arrest perpetrators’, Senate condemns political violence nationwide appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: AFCONQ: Why I didn’t invite Maduka Okoye – Chelle
item.description: Super Eagles head coach Eric Chelle has explained his decision to leave goalkeeper Maduka Okoye out of Nigeria’s squad for their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches. Chelle, who is preparing the Super Eagles for their double-header against Tanzania, said his selection decisions were based on considerations both on and off the pitch. The Franco-Malian tactician insisted that the national team was not obligated to any particular player, stressing that his choices were guided by his assessment of what was best for the squad. “The national team is not close to him or anyone. I made my choice and when I made my choice I made it around the pitch and outside it,” Chelle said. Okoye, who plays for Italian club Udinese, has been absent from recent Super Eagles selections, with Stanley Nwabali, Francis Uzoho and Arthur Okonkwo among the goalkeepers considered by the coach. Chelle’s latest comments underline his position that selection for the national team is based on his technical and other considerations rather than a player’s reputation or status. The Super Eagles are seeking to strengthen their position in the AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign as they prepare to face Tanzania in two crucial Group L encounters. item.title: AFCON 2027Q: Guinea-Bissau drop points, hand Super Eagles chance to close gap
item.description: Nigeria’s Super Eagles have received a boost in their quest to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations after Guinea-Bissau were held to a 1-1 draw by Madagascar in their Group L encounter on Thursday. The result offers Nigeria an opportunity to reduce the gap at the top of the group following Guinea-Bissau’s impressive start to the qualifying campaign. The Djurtus had taken control of Group L after recording a 3-0 victory over the Super Eagles in their Matchday Two encounter last month. However, they were unable to maintain their winning run against Madagascar, needing a late goal to salvage a point. Warren Caddy gave Madagascar the lead a minute before the hour mark, putting Guinea-Bissau under pressure. But Galatasaray forward Renato Nhaga came to the visitors’ rescue, scoring six minutes from time to secure a 1-1 draw. The result leaves Guinea-Bissau top of Group L with seven points from three matches, while Madagascar sit third with two points. Nigeria can take advantage of the dropped points when they host Tanzania’s Taifa Stars in Uyo on Friday. A victory would strengthen the Super Eagles’ position in the group and provide a much-needed boost to their qualification hopes after their heavy defeat to Guinea-Bissau. The encounter is therefore crucial for Nigeria as they seek to get their AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign back on track. item.title: 2027: Trust me, I won’t fail you, INEC chair assures Nigerians
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has asked Nigerians to trust him to deliver a free, fair, credible and inclusive election next year, promising to not fail them This was as he said the commission is yet to recover from the trust deficit created by the technical glitches associated with the 2023 general election, and vowed that inaccurate polling unit results will not reach the INEC Result Viewing Portal IReV in 2027. Amupitan spoke on Thursday at Chatham House, London, at a dialogue held with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI) on the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” His Chief Press Secretary, Adedayo Oketola, said the INEC chairman noted that the controversies over the 2023 presidential election badly dented public confidence in the commission. “First, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC—damage so large that the Commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said. He said the commission’s audit after 2023 traced the worst result management failures to collation centres, not polling units. “In 2023, there were instances of inaccurate results or results with over-voting being uploaded onto IReV. We have now devised a technical safeguard: if a result is not accurate at the polling unit, it will not go to IReV at all. The moment a result appears on IReV, citizens can trust what they see. By eliminating inconsistencies at the source, collation will become a transparent formality”, he stated. The INEC chairman announced that the commission would hold a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28, 2026. “On the 28th of this month, we will conduct a mock accreditation and voting exercise across all states of the federation to simulate the presidential election and verify that we have gotten both accreditation and electronic result transmission right,” he said. Asked why Nigerians should trust his leadership, Amupitan who assumed office in October 2025, pointed to the off-cycle elections he had conducted. “Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said. He listed the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, the Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections. The 2023 general election was a major lesson for Nigeria, and the Anambra election was another,” he said. item.title: Scaloni to stay on as Argentina coach until 2030 World Cup
item.description: Lionel Scaloni on Thursday agreed to stay on as coach of Argentina’s national football team until after the 2030 World Cup, ending the doubts that had been swirling since this year’s World Cup final defeat. Scaloni’s decision to renew his contract was announced by Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia at a press conference with the 48-year-old manager. Scaloni, who took the Albiceleste to victory at the 2022 tournament in Qatar, told reporters he was as enthusiastic as “on day one”. “A new project begins now,” he said a month after Lionel Messi, the team’s leading light for 20 years, bowed out of international football. Tapia said that Scaloni would be the Argentina manager with the most World Cups under his belt by the time his contract ended. Scaloni had cast doubt on his future with the team after Argentina’s 1-0 defeat by Spain in a bad-tempered July 19 World Cup final in New Jersey. He has been coach for eight years, taking over in September 2018, after a traumatic World Cup in Russia, where Argentina were eliminated in the round of 16. Scaloni took over one of the most prestigious jobs in football without any prior experience and built the team into one widely considered the best in Argentine history. Besides the 2022 World Cup he coached Argentina to two Copa America titles, in 2021 and 2024. He now faces the task of taking the team forward without his 39-year-old talisman Messi. “What must remain is this team spirit, this feeling of unity among the players and the people,” he said after losing the final to Spain. item.title: Man United closing in on Pochettino after sacking manager Carrick
item.description: United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is set to be appointed as the new manager of Manchester United after the struggling English giants sacked Michael Carrick on Thursday. Pochettino is expected to leave his role with the USA following their two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final on Saturday and Tuesday in a move that will see United trigger a release clause worth some $10 million to secure the Argentine’s services. Pochettino, who signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago, is due to hold a pre-match press conference on Friday. Former United captain Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish in the Premier League last season, but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are in the relegation zone. The club confirmed in a statement Thursday that it had parted ways with the 45-year-old, following mounting speculation he would be axed during the international break. “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions,” United said. “Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.” Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim’s acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal but, hampered by the club’s underwhelming recruitment in the summer transfer window, his side have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager’s tactics following a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club’s hierarchy over their lack of top-quality signings. Carrick’s final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away despite a paltry record of three wins from 15 games in all competitions this season. It is believed Carrick’s future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. – ‘Disgusting’ – Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. Carrick, who won multiple trophies as a midfielder in the club’s golden era under Alex Ferguson, is the seventh permanent manager to be dismissed by the club since the Scot retired in 2013. item.title: Kwara PDP Candidate Kawu Pledges ₦100bn Security Fund
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Kwara State, Sulaiman Bolakale Kawu, has pledged to establish a ₦100bn security trust fund and introduce a 13th-month salary for civil servants if elected governor in the 2027 governorship election. Kawu made the pledges in Ilorin during the public presentation of his manifesto, tagged The SBK Compact – Kwara People First, which outlines his proposed policies on security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and economic development. The former top civil servant also promised to create 200,000 youth employment opportunities and 5,000 enterprise opportunities annually, alongside a ₦19.2bn agricultural production fund to provide affordable financing and inputs to farmers and cooperatives. He said the proposed ₦100bn security trust fund would finance intelligence-led operations, strengthen community partnerships, equip security agencies and improve coordination among security formations to address insecurity across the state. Kawu said his decision to prioritise security was informed by his visit to Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area, where he witnessed the aftermath of attacks and the suffering of residents. Sulaiman Bolakale Kawu “One of the most painful experiences in my entire life was my visit to Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area of our state. I stood before the destruction. I saw blood on the ground. I witnessed firsthand the pain and fear of a traumatised community,” he said. He added that the experience reinforced his determination to ensure that residents could live and conduct their businesses without fear of attacks, kidnapping and other criminal activities. “As Governor, I will not rest or sleep when the life of any Kwaran is under threat,” the PDP candidate said. On workers’ welfare, Kawu promised to introduce a 13th-month salary for all civil servants in the state, assuring that salaries and other entitlements would be paid promptly. “As a retired public servant myself, I understand the sacrifices, expectations and challenges of workers. I will ensure the prompt and timely payment of salaries and other entitlements. Workers must not have to struggle or beg for what they have lawfully earned,” he said. The former civil servant also proposed a ₦9.6bn revolving loan scheme for market traders and another ₦9.6bn single-digit interest loan scheme for micro, small and medium-scale enterprises. He said his administration would establish a ₦3bn Women Enterprises and Empowerment Fund to provide affordable financing and business support to women-owned businesses, while at least 1,000 artisans would receive support grants annually. On grassroots development, Kawu promised to allocate ₦50m to each of the 193 wards in the state within the first 100 days of his administration, amounting to an initial commitment of ₦9.65bn.
